That is the most monstrous expenditure that I ever heard of the government making for a work that is not at all necessary. This dam is for the benefit of a lot of mill owners on the Grand river. I do not believe you collect the amount that they promised each year for the use of the water for running their mills and to make an expenditure of $12,000 for a purely private undertaking for the benefit of these parties without a particle of benefit in it for the country at large is most unjustifiable. You might as well give me a present of $12,000 as make such an expenditure as that.

I want to reduce that item to $3,001. At the same time I would not be acting fairly by my
hon. friend if I conveyed the impression that that was all, because there was an appropriation in the main estimates for this work. This is only the balance.

What is the total
amount you are expending ?
There has been voted $30,000 and when we reduce this amount to $3,001 it will make $33,001.
And that is only for the purpose of repair ?
This finishes it.
This is being done by day labour ?
No, it is under contract. The contractors being Messrs. Hutchison, Lattimore & Lalor.
A great portion of it was done by day work.
I am advised that the hon. gentleman is mistaken.
Was there none done by day labour ?

The amount of the contract is stated to be $39,-069.9C, let to the lowest tenderers, the gentlemen whose names I have mentioned. It is a schedule contract and it is estimated to figure out to that amount.
That is all the expenditure under contract ?.
Yes.

Well, that is supplementary to the work done by the day there. There has been a lot of work done by day labour. There have been parties employed from 1896 down by the day for the purpose of renewing the dam.
In this case we are rebuilding the dam. The hon. gentleman is referring to some previous work of repair.
Rebuilding, is repairs.
This was commenced last year out of the appropriation of last year.
Is the object of this dam to furnish water to the feeder of the Welland canal which is not used at all now ?
What did Cayuga bridge cost ?
The hon. gentleman (Hon. Mr. Paterson) ought to know because he criticised it very severely when it was up in the House several years ago.
How much did that cost ?

speakerposition: Chief Opposition Whip; Whip of the Conservative Party (1867-1942)
speechtext: About $4,700.
A little more than that.
Look at the Auditor General's Report.
This is on the same ground. The river flooded the land.
What is the use of this dam to the public V
The information furnished me does not enable me to answer the hon. gentleman's question.
It is possible it may have some public utility but it is not apparent to any one who has visited the place. It may be apparent to the department.

I must confess that we are passing these large items very flippantly. It was necessary at one time to have this as a feeder to the Welland Canal, but it is not required since the canal was deepened, and why should the ratepayers of my riding be called upon to pay $33,000 to keep up a dam which is absolutely only for the use of private individuals who have mills along there ? If these private parties want a dam let them keep it up themselves.
The water must be maintained there and these parties have leases and pay us a revenue.	[DOT]
Let them have it free and keep the dam themselves.

It might be cheaper for the manufacturers to do that than to pay the considerable rental which they pay. We must remember that indirectly we are helping these manufacturers who have their works along the canal and who give employment to a large number of people. That is for the benefit of the public as a whole.

What is the amount of revenue the government receives? There were two flour mills there, one of which was burned down, and the one remaining turns out about 20 barrels a day. There is also a company manufacturing light for the town of Dunnville, and that is all. What revenue is paid by these people to the government ?

I will have it looked up, and give the hon. gentleman the information later.
Intercolonial Railway, operating expenses,
This simply refers to the increased volume of business.
You want it to balance your books.
Yes. I will bring down a statement of the receipts and expenditures later on, and we will pass the item with that understanding.

Very well.
